title: Integral of the Gaussian product density Hessian
statement:
Let $I$ be a finite index set, let $v>0$, let $c\in\mathbb R^I$, and let $f:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ be measurable with $|f(z)|\le1$ for every $z$. Let $Z$ have independent coordinates with $Z_k\sim N(c_k,v)$. The integral, with respect to Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R^I$, of $f(z)$ times the product Gaussian mean Hessian equals
\[\sum_{i,j\in I}\mathbb E\!\left[\left(\frac{(Z_i-c_i)(Z_j-c_j)}{v^2}-\frac{\mathbf 1_{i=j}}{v}\right)f(Z)\right] (e_j^*\otimes e_i^*),\]
where $e_k^*$ is the coordinate projection $z\mapsto z_k$, and $e_j^*\otimes e_i^*$ denotes the bilinear form $(h,k)\mapsto h_jk_i$.
replaced: Let $I$ be finite and $v\ge0$. Put $G_v(c,z)=\prod_i p_v(c_i,z_i)$, where $p_v$ is the Gaussian density of variance $v$ for $v>0$ and $p_0=0$, and put $S_v(c,z)[h]=\sum_i((z_i-c_i)/v)h_i$, with division by zero equal to zero. Define $A_v(c,z)[h]=G_v(c,z)S_v(c,z)[h]$ and $T_v(c,z)[h,k]=G_v(c,z)(S_v(c,z)[h]S_v(c,z)[k]-\sum_i h_i k_i/v)$. Let $f:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ be measurable with $|f|\le1$. If $v>0$, $c,h,k\in\mathbb R^I$, and $Z\sim\bigotimes_iN(c_i,v)$, then $(\int f(z)T_v(c,z)\,dz)[h,k]=\sum_{i,j}\mathbb E[((Z_i-c_i)(Z_j-c_j)/v^2-\delta_{ij}/v)f(Z)]h_jk_i$, where $\delta_{ij}$ is the Kronecker delta.
